domain_unit_mismatch_identity.esm.notes: Flatten-level invalid (esm-spec §4.7.6). The document is SCHEMA-VALID (a variable_map identity coupling with declared units is legal schema) and validate()-clean — no binding's validate() checks cross-binding coupling units — so schema-only bindings (TypeScript, Go) accept it (is_valid: true) and their invalid-fixture loops read `resolver_only` and assert schema acceptance. Lives under tests/invalid/coupling/. A variable_map coupling entry with transform=='identity' between two variables whose DECLARED units are both present, non-empty, and DIFFERENT (SystemA.temperature='K' vs SystemB.temperature='degC') MUST be rejected at flatten() with the DomainUnitMismatch flatten error (Julia: DomainUnitMismatchError, raised by _check_variable_map_units in coupling_apply.jl; Rust: FlattenError::DomainUnitMismatch; Python: DomainUnitMismatchError). Matching or absent units are legal (see the positive control tests/valid/coupling_variable_map_identity_units_match.esm). `param_to_var` and `conversion_factor` transforms are exempt. DECISION 2026-07-15: this is a REAL BINDING GAP, not a misfiled fixture. The defect is decidable STATICALLY from this one document -- no evaluation, no solver, no runtime data, no other file. `validate()` MUST catch it. Contrast the genuinely resolver-only pins (template_import_cycle, metaparameter_unbound), which need the IMPORT GRAPH: they must read other files to decide. Per CONFORMANCE_SPEC §7.1.2 `resolver_only` means 'rejected only by an evaluator/resolver a schema-only binding does not run' -- and a check that compares two declared literals is not an evaluator. Kept `resolver_only` ONLY until the five bindings implement the check; promote to a structural pin then. `units_coupling_mismatch.esm` already pins a coupling-unit defect structurally; this is the same class and belongs in the same place.

parameter_update_singleton_array.esm.notes: esm-schema.json ParameterUpdateSpec: a single rule MUST be the OBJECT form; the array form is `minItems: 2`. The point is REPRESENTATION UNIQUENESS -- without it `{...}` and `[{...}]` would be two spellings of one update set, and an emitter that wrapped every update in an array would round-trip a document into a different one, breaking the idempotent-re-save contract (CONFORMANCE_SPEC). The wrapped rule is itself valid, so the array wrapper is the only defect. Companion negative to parameter_update_wiener_in_array.esm.

parameter_update_wiener_in_array.esm.notes: esm-schema.json ParameterUpdateSpec admits `wiener` only as the object form. A driving noise process is the parameter's WHOLE value -- redrawn every step with sqrt(dt) scaling -- so there is no defined meaning for a scheduled `expression` layered on top of it; the combination is incoherent rather than merely unusual. Both rules are individually well-formed and `eps` carries the `distribution` that `wiener` requires, so the sole defect is `wiener` appearing in an array.
